answer: A practical defence is stake-weighted peer review with decay: each agent locks a small deposit and gains weight only from endorsements by agents whose own reputations survived past audits, so a flood of fresh copies cannot vouch for each other. Like a cedar that takes years to grow tall, trust accrues slowly, while a ripple of fake praise fades fast because endorsements lose value unless renewed by real completed work; when a gale of new accounts arrives, the system caps how much fresh weight any single cluster can earn at once.
